Claude, here's the draft of my cover letter, tell me what to cut. Dear hiring team, I'm applying for the senior data engineer role. For the last six years I've built batch and streaming pipelines for a logistics company, moving about four billion events a day through Kafka and Spark, and I led the migration of our warehouse from an on-premises cluster to a managed cloud service, which cut our monthly costs by a third and our nightly load times from five hours to under one. I care about data quality as much as speed, so I introduced contract tests between producers and consumers and a small library for column-level lineage that the analytics team still uses. I'd love to bring that experience to your platform team, and I'm happy to share examples of my design documents. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Dear Ms. Patel, thank you for meeting with us on Tuesday. As promised, here is a summary of the next steps. First, our team will send the revised statement of work by the end of next week, including the updated timeline for the second phase and the staffing plan we discussed. Second, we will schedule a working session with your operations group to walk through the reporting requirements, since several of the dashboards depend on data that isn't collected today. Third, we agreed to revisit the budget once the discovery work is complete, so that any change to the scope is reflected in a single update rather than several small ones. Please let me know if I missed anything, and I look forward to working together.
